41 /// A life support system for temporary objects created by `type_caster::load()`.
42 /// Adding a patient will keep it alive up until the enclosing function returns.
43 class loader_life_support {
44 private:
45 // Thread-local top-of-stack for loader_life_support frames (linked via parent).
46 // Observation: loader_life_support needs to be thread-local,
47 // but we don't need to go to extra effort to keep it
48 // per-interpreter (i.e., by putting it in internals) since
49 // individual function calls are already isolated to a single
50 // interpreter, even though they could potentially call into a
51 // different interpreter later in the same call chain. This
52 // saves a significant cost per function call spent in
53 // loader_life_support destruction.
54 // Note for future C++17 simplification:
55 // inline static thread_local loader_life_support *tls_current_frame = nullptr;
56 ✗ static loader_life_support *&tls_current_frame() {
57 static thread_local loader_life_support *frame_ptr = nullptr;
58 ✗ return frame_ptr;
59 }
60
61 loader_life_support *parent = nullptr;
62 std::unordered_set<PyObject *> keep_alive;
63
64 public:
65 /// A new patient frame is created when a function is entered
66 ✗ loader_life_support() {
67 ✗ auto &frame = tls_current_frame();
68 ✗ parent = frame;
69 ✗ frame = this;
70 ✗ }
71
72 /// ... and destroyed after it returns
73 ✗ ~loader_life_support() {
74 ✗ auto &frame = tls_current_frame();
75 ✗ if (frame != this) {
76 ✗ pybind11_fail("loader_life_support: internal error");
77 }
78 ✗ frame = parent;
79 ✗ for (auto *item : keep_alive) {
80 Py_DECREF(item);

82 ✗ }

87 ✗ loader_life_support *frame = tls_current_frame();
88 ✗ if (!frame) {
89 // NOTE: It would be nice to include the stack frames here, as this indicates
90 // use of pybind11::cast<> outside the normal call framework, finding such
91 // a location is challenging. Developers could consider printing out
92 // stack frame addresses here using something like __builtin_frame_address(0)
93 ✗ throw cast_error("When called outside a bound function, py::cast() cannot "
94 "do Python -> C++ conversions which require the creation "

98 ✗ if (frame->keep_alive.insert(h.ptr()).second) {

114 ✗ type_info *existing_base = *it;

292 ✗ inline bool try_incref(PyObject *obj) {
293 // Tries to increment the reference count of an object if it's not zero.
294 #if defined(Py_GIL_DISABLED) && PY_VERSION_HEX >= 0x030E00A4
295 return PyUnstable_TryIncRef(obj);
296 #elif defined(Py_GIL_DISABLED)
297 // See
298 // https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d05140f9f77d7dfc753dd1e5ac3a5962aaa03eff/Include/internal/pycore_object.h#L761
299 uint32_t local = _Py_atomic_load_uint32_relaxed(&obj->ob_ref_local);
300 local += 1;
301 if (local == 0) {
302 // immortal
303 return true;
304 }
305 if (_Py_IsOwnedByCurrentThread(obj)) {
306 _Py_atomic_store_uint32_relaxed(&obj->ob_ref_local, local);
307 # ifdef Py_REF_DEBUG
308 _Py_INCREF_IncRefTotal();
309 # endif
310 return true;
311 }
312 Py_ssize_t shared = _Py_atomic_load_ssize_relaxed(&obj->ob_ref_shared);
313 for (;;) {
314 // If the shared refcount is zero and the object is either merged
315 // or may not have weak references, then we cannot incref it.
316 if (shared == 0 || shared == _Py_REF_MERGED) {
317 return false;
318 }
319
320 if (_Py_atomic_compare_exchange_ssize(
321 &obj->ob_ref_shared, &shared, shared + (1 << _Py_REF_SHARED_SHIFT))) {
322 # ifdef Py_REF_DEBUG
323 _Py_INCREF_IncRefTotal();
324 # endif
325 return true;
326 }
327 }
328 #else
329 ✗ assert(Py_REFCNT(obj) > 0);
330 Py_INCREF(obj);
331 ✗ return true;
332 #endif
333 }

335 // Searches the inheritance graph for a registered Python instance, using all_type_info().
336 ✗ PYBIND11_NOINLINE handle find_registered_python_instance(void *src,

338 ✗ return with_instance_map(src, [&](instance_map &instances) {
339 ✗ auto it_instances = instances.equal_range(src);
340 ✗ for (auto it_i = it_instances.first; it_i != it_instances.second; ++it_i) {
341 ✗ for (auto *instance_type : detail::all_type_info(Py_TYPE(it_i->second))) {
342 ✗ if (instance_type && same_type(*instance_type->cpptype, *tinfo->cpptype)) {
343 ✗ auto *wrapper = reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(it_i->second);
344 ✗ if (try_incref(wrapper)) {
345 ✗ return handle(wrapper);
346 }
347 }
348 }
349 }
350 ✗ return handle();
351 ✗ });
352 }

548 // Information about how type_caster_generic::cast() can obtain its source object
549 struct cast_sources {
550 // A type-erased pointer and the type it points to
551 struct raw_source {
552 const void *cppobj;
553 const std::type_info *cpptype;
554 };
555
556 // A C++ pointer and the Python type info we will convert it to;
557 // we expect that cppobj points to something of type tinfo->cpptype
558 struct resolved_source {
559 const void *cppobj;
560 const type_info *tinfo;
561 };
562
563 // Use the given pointer with its compile-time type, possibly downcast
564 // via polymorphic_type_hook()
565 template <typename itype>
566 explicit cast_sources(const itype *ptr);
567
568 // Use the given pointer and type
569 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(google-explicit-constructor)
570 cast_sources(const raw_source &orig) : original(orig) { result = resolve(); }
571
572 // Use the given object and pybind11 type info. NB: if tinfo is null,
573 // this does not provide enough information to use a foreign type or
574 // to render a useful error message
575 cast_sources(const void *obj, const detail::type_info *tinfo)
576 : original{obj, tinfo ? tinfo->cpptype : nullptr}, result{obj, tinfo} {}
577
578 // The object passed to cast(), with its static type.
579 // original.type must not be null if resolve() will be called.
580 // original.obj may be null if we're converting nullptr to a Python None
581 raw_source original;
582
583 // A more-derived version of `original` provided by a
584 // polymorphic_type_hook. downcast.type may be null if this is not
585 // a relevant concept for the current cast.
586 raw_source downcast{};
587
588 // The source to use for this cast, and the corresponding pybind11
589 // type_info. If the type_info is null, then pybind11 doesn't know
590 // about this type.
591 resolved_source result;
592
593 // Returns true if the cast will use a pybind11 type that uses
594 // a smart holder.
595 bool creates_smart_holder() const {
596 return result.tinfo != nullptr
597 && result.tinfo->holder_enum_v == detail::holder_enum_t::smart_holder;
598 }
599
600 private:
601 ✗ resolved_source resolve() {
602 ✗ if (downcast.cpptype) {
603 ✗ if (same_type(*original.cpptype, *downcast.cpptype)) {
604 ✗ downcast.cpptype = nullptr;
605 ✗ } else if (const auto *tpi = get_type_info(*downcast.cpptype)) {
606 ✗ return {downcast.cppobj, tpi};
607 }
608 }
609 ✗ if (const auto *tpi = get_type_info(*original.cpptype)) {
610 ✗ return {original.cppobj, tpi};
611 }
612 ✗ return {nullptr, nullptr};
613 }
614 };

674 template <typename T, typename D>
675 handle smart_holder_from_unique_ptr(std::unique_ptr<T, D> &&src,
676 return_value_policy policy,
677 handle parent,
678 const cast_sources::resolved_source &cs) {
679 if (policy == return_value_policy::copy) {
680 throw cast_error("return_value_policy::copy is invalid for unique_ptr.");
681 }
682 if (!src) {
683 return none().release();
684 }
685 // cs.cppobj is the subobject pointer appropriate for tinfo (may differ from src.get()
686 // under MI/VI). Use this for Python identity/registration, but keep ownership on T*.
687 void *src_raw_void_ptr = const_cast<void *>(cs.cppobj);
688 assert(cs.tinfo != nullptr);
689 const detail::type_info *tinfo = cs.tinfo;
690 if (handle existing_inst = find_registered_python_instance(src_raw_void_ptr, tinfo)) {
691 auto *self_life_support = tinfo->get_trampoline_self_life_support(src.get());
692 if (self_life_support != nullptr) {
693 value_and_holder &v_h = self_life_support->v_h;
694 if (v_h.inst != nullptr && v_h.vh != nullptr) {
695 auto &holder = v_h.holder<smart_holder>();
696 if (!holder.is_disowned) {
697 pybind11_fail("smart_holder_from_unique_ptr: unexpected "
698 "smart_holder.is_disowned failure.");
699 }
700 // Critical transfer-of-ownership section. This must stay together.
701 self_life_support->deactivate_life_support();
702 holder.reclaim_disowned(tinfo->get_memory_guarded_delete);
703 (void) src.release();
704 // Critical section end.
705 return existing_inst;
706 }
707 }
708 throw cast_error("Invalid unique_ptr: another instance owns this pointer already.");
709 }
710
711 auto inst = reinterpret_steal<object>(make_new_instance(tinfo->type));
712 auto *inst_raw_ptr = reinterpret_cast<instance *>(inst.ptr());
713 inst_raw_ptr->owned = true;
714 void *&valueptr = values_and_holders(inst_raw_ptr).begin()->value_ptr();
715 valueptr = src_raw_void_ptr;
716
717 if (static_cast<void *>(src.get()) == src_raw_void_ptr) {
718 // This is a multiple-inheritance situation that is incompatible with the current
719 // shared_from_this handling (see PR #3023). Is there a better solution?
720 src_raw_void_ptr = nullptr;
721 }
722 auto smhldr = smart_holder::from_unique_ptr(std::move(src), src_raw_void_ptr);
723 tinfo->init_instance(inst_raw_ptr, static_cast<const void *>(&smhldr));
724
725 if (policy == return_value_policy::reference_internal) {
726 keep_alive_impl(inst, parent);
727 }
728
729 return inst.release();
730 }
731
732 template <typename T, typename D>
733 handle smart_holder_from_unique_ptr(std::unique_ptr<T const, D> &&src,
734 return_value_policy policy,
735 handle parent,
736 const cast_sources::resolved_source &cs) {
737 return smart_holder_from_unique_ptr(
738 std::unique_ptr<T, D>(const_cast<T *>(src.release()),
739 std::move(src.get_deleter())), // Const2Mutbl
740 policy,
741 parent,
742 cs);

745 template <typename T>
746 handle smart_holder_from_shared_ptr(const std::shared_ptr<T> &src,
747 return_value_policy policy,
748 handle parent,
749 const cast_sources::resolved_source &cs) {
750 switch (policy) {
751 case return_value_policy::automatic:
752 case return_value_policy::automatic_reference:
753 break;
754 case return_value_policy::take_ownership:
755 throw cast_error("Invalid return_value_policy for shared_ptr (take_ownership).");
756 case return_value_policy::copy:
757 case return_value_policy::move:
758 break;
759 case return_value_policy::reference:
760 throw cast_error("Invalid return_value_policy for shared_ptr (reference).");
761 case return_value_policy::reference_internal:
762 break;
763 }
764 if (!src) {
765 return none().release();
766 }
767
768 // cs.cppobj is the subobject pointer appropriate for tinfo (may differ from src.get()
769 // under MI/VI). Use this for Python identity/registration, but keep ownership on T*.
770 void *src_raw_void_ptr = const_cast<void *>(cs.cppobj);
771 assert(cs.tinfo != nullptr);
772 const detail::type_info *tinfo = cs.tinfo;
773 if (handle existing_inst = find_registered_python_instance(src_raw_void_ptr, tinfo)) {
774 // PYBIND11:REMINDER: MISSING: Enforcement of consistency with existing smart_holder.
775 // PYBIND11:REMINDER: MISSING: keep_alive.
776 return existing_inst;
777 }
778
779 auto inst = reinterpret_steal<object>(make_new_instance(tinfo->type));
780 auto *inst_raw_ptr = reinterpret_cast<instance *>(inst.ptr());
781 inst_raw_ptr->owned = true;
782 void *&valueptr = values_and_holders(inst_raw_ptr).begin()->value_ptr();
783 valueptr = src_raw_void_ptr;
784
785 auto smhldr = smart_holder::from_shared_ptr(std::shared_ptr<void>(src, src_raw_void_ptr));
786 tinfo->init_instance(inst_raw_ptr, static_cast<const void *>(&smhldr));
787
788 if (policy == return_value_policy::reference_internal) {
789 keep_alive_impl(inst, parent);
790 }
791
792 return inst.release();
793 }

868 std::shared_ptr<T> load_as_shared_ptr(const type_info *tinfo,
869 void *void_raw_ptr,
870 handle responsible_parent = nullptr,
871 // to support py::potentially_slicing_weak_ptr
872 // with minimal added code complexity:
873 bool force_potentially_slicing_shared_ptr
874 = false) const {
875 if (!have_holder()) {
876 return nullptr;
877 }
878 throw_if_uninitialized_or_disowned_holder(typeid(T));
879 smart_holder &hld = holder();
880 hld.ensure_is_not_disowned("load_as_shared_ptr");
881 if (hld.vptr_is_using_noop_deleter) {
882 if (responsible_parent) {
883 return make_shared_ptr_with_responsible_parent(static_cast<T *>(void_raw_ptr),
884 responsible_parent);
885 }
886 throw std::runtime_error("Non-owning holder (load_as_shared_ptr).");
887 }
888 auto *type_raw_ptr = static_cast<T *>(void_raw_ptr);
889 if (python_instance_is_alias && !force_potentially_slicing_shared_ptr) {
890 auto *vptr_gd_ptr = tinfo->get_memory_guarded_delete(holder().vptr);
891 if (vptr_gd_ptr != nullptr) {
892 std::shared_ptr<void> released_ptr = vptr_gd_ptr->released_ptr.lock();
893 if (released_ptr) {
894 return std::shared_ptr<T>(released_ptr, type_raw_ptr);
895 }
896 std::shared_ptr<T> to_be_released(
897 type_raw_ptr, shared_ptr_trampoline_self_life_support(loaded_v_h.inst));
898 vptr_gd_ptr->released_ptr = to_be_released;
899 return to_be_released;
900 }
901 auto *sptsls_ptr = std::get_deleter<shared_ptr_trampoline_self_life_support>(hld.vptr);
902 if (sptsls_ptr != nullptr) {
903 // This code is reachable only if there are multiple registered_instances for the
904 // same pointee.
905 if (reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(loaded_v_h.inst) == sptsls_ptr->self) {
906 pybind11_fail("smart_holder_type_caster_support load_as_shared_ptr failure: "
907 "loaded_v_h.inst == sptsls_ptr->self");
908 }
909 }
910 if (sptsls_ptr != nullptr || !memory::type_has_shared_from_this(type_raw_ptr)) {
911 return std::shared_ptr<T>(
912 type_raw_ptr, shared_ptr_trampoline_self_life_support(loaded_v_h.inst));
913 }
914 if (hld.vptr_is_external_shared_ptr) {
915 pybind11_fail("smart_holder_type_casters load_as_shared_ptr failure: not "
916 "implemented: trampoline-self-life-support for external shared_ptr "
917 "to type inheriting from std::enable_shared_from_this.");
918 }
919 pybind11_fail(
920 "smart_holder_type_casters: load_as_shared_ptr failure: internal inconsistency.");
921 }
922 std::shared_ptr<void> void_shd_ptr = hld.template as_shared_ptr<void>();
923 return std::shared_ptr<T>(void_shd_ptr, type_raw_ptr);
924 }

926 template <typename D>
927 std::unique_ptr<T, D> load_as_unique_ptr(const type_info *tinfo,
928 void *raw_void_ptr,
929 const char *context = "load_as_unique_ptr") {
930 if (!have_holder()) {
931 return unique_with_deleter<T, D>(nullptr, std::unique_ptr<D>());
932 }
933 throw_if_uninitialized_or_disowned_holder(typeid(T));
934 throw_if_instance_is_currently_owned_by_shared_ptr(tinfo);
935 holder().ensure_is_not_disowned(context);
936 holder().template ensure_compatible_uqp_del<T, D>(context);
937 holder().ensure_use_count_1(context);
938
939 T *raw_type_ptr = static_cast<T *>(raw_void_ptr);
940
941 auto *self_life_support = tinfo->get_trampoline_self_life_support(raw_type_ptr);
942 // This is enforced indirectly by a static_assert in the class_ implementation:
943 assert(!python_instance_is_alias || self_life_support);
944
945 std::unique_ptr<D> extracted_deleter
946 = holder().template extract_deleter<T, D>(context, tinfo->get_memory_guarded_delete);
947
948 // Critical transfer-of-ownership section. This must stay together.
949 if (self_life_support != nullptr) {
950 holder().disown(tinfo->get_memory_guarded_delete);
951 } else {
952 holder().release_ownership(tinfo->get_memory_guarded_delete);
953 }
954 auto result = unique_with_deleter<T, D>(raw_type_ptr, std::move(extracted_deleter));
955 if (self_life_support != nullptr) {
956 self_life_support->activate_life_support(loaded_v_h);
957 } else {
958 void *value_void_ptr = loaded_v_h.value_ptr();
959 loaded_v_h.value_ptr() = nullptr;
960 deregister_instance(loaded_v_h.inst, value_void_ptr, loaded_v_h.type);
961 }
962 // Critical section end.
963
964 return result;
965 }

967 // This assumes load_as_shared_ptr succeeded(), and the returned shared_ptr is still alive.
968 // The returned unique_ptr is meant to never expire (the behavior is undefined otherwise).
969 template <typename D>
970 std::unique_ptr<T, D> load_as_const_unique_ptr(const type_info *tinfo,
971 T *raw_type_ptr,
972 const char *context
973 = "load_as_const_unique_ptr") {
974 if (!have_holder()) {
975 return unique_with_deleter<T, D>(nullptr, std::unique_ptr<D>());
976 }
977 holder().template ensure_compatible_uqp_del<T, D>(context);

1242 ✗ this_.load_value(

1332 /**
1333 * Determine suitable casting operator for pointer-or-lvalue-casting type casters. The type caster
1334 * needs to provide `operator T*()` and `operator T&()` operators.
1335 *
1336 * If the type supports moving the value away via an `operator T&&() &&` method, it should use
1337 * `movable_cast_op_type` instead.
1338 */
1339 template <typename T>
1340 using cast_op_type = conditional_t<std::is_pointer<remove_reference_t<T>>::value,
1341 typename std::add_pointer<intrinsic_t<T>>::type,
1342 typename std::add_lvalue_reference<intrinsic_t<T>>::type>;
1343
1344 /**
1345 * Determine suitable casting operator for a type caster with a movable value. Such a type caster
1346 * needs to provide `operator T*()`, `operator T&()`, and `operator T&&() &&`. The latter will be
1347 * called in appropriate contexts where the value can be moved rather than copied.
1348 *
1349 * These operator are automatically provided when using the PYBIND11_TYPE_CASTER macro.
1350 */
1351 template <typename T>
1352 using movable_cast_op_type
1353 = conditional_t<std::is_pointer<typename std::remove_reference<T>::type>::value,
1354 typename std::add_pointer<intrinsic_t<T>>::type,
1355 conditional_t<std::is_rvalue_reference<T>::value,
1356 typename std::add_rvalue_reference<intrinsic_t<T>>::type,
1357 typename std::add_lvalue_reference<intrinsic_t<T>>::type>>;
1358
1359 // Does the container have a mapped type and is it recursive?
1360 // Implemented by specializations below.
1361 template <typename Container, typename SFINAE = void>
1362 struct container_mapped_type_traits {
1363 static constexpr bool has_mapped_type = false;
1364 static constexpr bool has_recursive_mapped_type = false;
1365 };
1366
1367 template <typename Container>
1368 struct container_mapped_type_traits<
1369 Container,
1370 typename std::enable_if<
1371 std::is_same<typename Container::mapped_type, Container>::value>::type> {
1372 static constexpr bool has_mapped_type = true;
1373 static constexpr bool has_recursive_mapped_type = true;
1374 };
1375
1376 template <typename Container>
1377 struct container_mapped_type_traits<
1378 Container,
1379 typename std::enable_if<
1380 negation<std::is_same<typename Container::mapped_type, Container>>::value>::type> {
1381 static constexpr bool has_mapped_type = true;
1382 static constexpr bool has_recursive_mapped_type = false;
1383 };
1384
1385 // Does the container have a value type and is it recursive?
1386 // Implemented by specializations below.
1387 template <typename Container, typename SFINAE = void>
1388 struct container_value_type_traits : std::false_type {
1389 static constexpr bool has_value_type = false;
1390 static constexpr bool has_recursive_value_type = false;
1391 };
1392
1393 template <typename Container>
1394 struct container_value_type_traits<
1395 Container,
1396 typename std::enable_if<
1397 std::is_same<typename Container::value_type, Container>::value>::type> {
1398 static constexpr bool has_value_type = true;
1399 static constexpr bool has_recursive_value_type = true;
1400 };
1401
1402 template <typename Container>
1403 struct container_value_type_traits<
1404 Container,
1405 typename std::enable_if<
1406 negation<std::is_same<typename Container::value_type, Container>>::value>::type> {
1407 static constexpr bool has_value_type = true;
1408 static constexpr bool has_recursive_value_type = false;
1409 };
1410
1411 /*
1412 * Tag to be used for representing the bottom of recursively defined types.
1413 * Define this tag so we don't have to use void.
1414 */
1415 struct recursive_bottom {};
1416
1417 /*
1418 * Implementation detail of `recursive_container_traits` below.
1419 * `T` is the `value_type` of the container, which might need to be modified to
1420 * avoid recursive types and const types.
1421 */
1422 template <typename T, bool is_this_a_map>
1423 struct impl_type_to_check_recursively {
1424 /*
1425 * If the container is recursive, then no further recursion should be done.
1426 */
1427 using if_recursive = recursive_bottom;
1428 /*
1429 * Otherwise yield `T` unchanged.
1430 */
1431 using if_not_recursive = T;
1432 };
1433
1434 /*
1435 * For pairs - only as value type of a map -, the first type should remove the `const`.
1436 * Also, if the map is recursive, then the recursive checking should consider
1437 * the first type only.
1438 */
1439 template <typename A, typename B>
1440 struct impl_type_to_check_recursively<std::pair<A, B>, /* is_this_a_map = */ true> {
1441 using if_recursive = typename std::remove_const<A>::type;
1442 using if_not_recursive = std::pair<typename std::remove_const<A>::type, B>;
1443 };
1444
1445 /*
1446 * Implementation of `recursive_container_traits` below.
1447 */
1448 template <typename Container, typename SFINAE = void>
1449 struct impl_recursive_container_traits {
1450 using type_to_check_recursively = recursive_bottom;
1451 };
1452
1453 template <typename Container>
1454 struct impl_recursive_container_traits<
1455 Container,
1456 typename std::enable_if<container_value_type_traits<Container>::has_value_type>::type> {
1457 static constexpr bool is_recursive
1458 = container_mapped_type_traits<Container>::has_recursive_mapped_type
1459 || container_value_type_traits<Container>::has_recursive_value_type;
1460 /*
1461 * This member dictates which type Pybind11 should check recursively in traits
1462 * such as `is_move_constructible`, `is_copy_constructible`, `is_move_assignable`, ...
1463 * Direct access to `value_type` should be avoided:
1464 * 1. `value_type` might recursively contain the type again
1465 * 2. `value_type` of STL map types is `std::pair<A const, B>`, the `const`
1466 * should be removed.
1467 *
1468 */
1469 using type_to_check_recursively = typename std::conditional<
1470 is_recursive,
1471 typename impl_type_to_check_recursively<
1472 typename Container::value_type,
1473 container_mapped_type_traits<Container>::has_mapped_type>::if_recursive,
1474 typename impl_type_to_check_recursively<
1475 typename Container::value_type,
1476 container_mapped_type_traits<Container>::has_mapped_type>::if_not_recursive>::type;
1477 };
1478
1479 /*
1480 * This trait defines the `type_to_check_recursively` which is needed to properly
1481 * handle recursively defined traits such as `is_move_constructible` without going
1482 * into an infinite recursion.
1483 * Should be used instead of directly accessing the `value_type`.
1484 * It cancels the recursion by returning the `recursive_bottom` tag.
1485 *
1486 * The default definition of `type_to_check_recursively` is as follows:
1487 *
1488 * 1. By default, it is `recursive_bottom`, so that the recursion is canceled.
1489 * 2. If the type is non-recursive and defines a `value_type`, then the `value_type` is used.
1490 * If the `value_type` is a pair and a `mapped_type` is defined,
1491 * then the `const` is removed from the first type.
1492 * 3. If the type is recursive and `value_type` is not a pair, then `recursive_bottom` is returned.
1493 * 4. If the type is recursive and `value_type` is a pair and a `mapped_type` is defined,
1494 * then `const` is removed from the first type and the first type is returned.
1495 *
1496 * This behavior can be extended by the user as seen in test_stl_binders.cpp.
1497 *
1498 * This struct is exactly the same as impl_recursive_container_traits.
1499 * The duplication achieves that user-defined specializations don't compete
1500 * with internal specializations, but take precedence.
1501 */
1502 template <typename Container, typename SFINAE = void>
1503 struct recursive_container_traits : impl_recursive_container_traits<Container> {};
1504
1505 template <typename T>
1506 struct is_move_constructible
1507 : all_of<std::is_move_constructible<T>,
1508 is_move_constructible<
1509 typename recursive_container_traits<T>::type_to_check_recursively>> {};
1510
1511 template <>
1512 struct is_move_constructible<recursive_bottom> : std::true_type {};

1514 // Likewise for std::pair

1516 // themselves move constructible, but this can not be relied upon when T1 or T2 are themselves
1517 // containers).

1519 struct is_move_constructible<std::pair<T1, T2>>
1520 : all_of<is_move_constructible<T1>, is_move_constructible<T2>> {};

1533 // Likewise for std::pair

1558 // polymorphic_type_hook<itype>::get(src, tinfo) determines whether the object pointed
1559 // to by `src` actually is an instance of some class derived from `itype`.
1560 // If so, it sets `tinfo` to point to the std::type_info representing that derived
1561 // type, and returns a pointer to the start of the most-derived object of that type
1562 // (in which `src` is a subobject; this will be the same address as `src` in most
1563 // single inheritance cases). If not, or if `src` is nullptr, it simply returns `src`
1564 // and leaves `tinfo` at its default value of nullptr.
1565 //
1566 // The default polymorphic_type_hook just returns src. A specialization for polymorphic
1567 // types determines the runtime type of the passed object and adjusts the this-pointer
1568 // appropriately via dynamic_cast<void*>. This is what enables a C++ Animal* to appear
1569 // to Python as a Dog (if Dog inherits from Animal, Animal is polymorphic, Dog is
1570 // registered with pybind11, and this Animal is in fact a Dog).
1571 //
1572 // You may specialize polymorphic_type_hook yourself for types that want to appear
1573 // polymorphic to Python but do not use C++ RTTI. (This is a not uncommon pattern
1574 // in performance-sensitive applications, used most notably in LLVM.)
1575 //
1576 // polymorphic_type_hook_base allows users to specialize polymorphic_type_hook with
1577 // std::enable_if. User provided specializations will always have higher priority than
1578 // the default implementation and specialization provided in polymorphic_type_hook_base.
1579 template <typename itype, typename SFINAE = void>
1580 struct polymorphic_type_hook_base {
1581 ✗ static const void *get(const itype *src, const std::type_info *&) { return src; }
1582 };
1583 template <typename itype>
1584 struct polymorphic_type_hook_base<itype, detail::enable_if_t<std::is_polymorphic<itype>::value>> {
1585 ✗ static const void *get(const itype *src, const std::type_info *&type) {
1586 ✗ type = src ? &typeid(*src) : nullptr;
1587 ✗ return dynamic_cast<const void *>(src);
1588 }
1589 };
1590 template <typename itype, typename SFINAE = void>
1591 struct polymorphic_type_hook : public polymorphic_type_hook_base<itype> {};
